main_text.p: tiæ signum est, quàm si quis ex pulcherrimo cubiculo vel cœnaculo faceret hará, vel stabulum equorum. Quis ergo tales sana mente vti dicat? Eadè est ebrietatis ratio. Vt primùm enim vinum immodicè haustu fuerit, mox rationis lumine obscurato, lingua sibi ad conuitia, blasphemias, obscœna dicta & promissa incauta habenas laxat, oculi circa formas alienas vagantur, manus ad arma promptæ sunt, & brutis animalibus vel impudetia, vel ferocitate, vel stultitia similis redditur, qui illis præstare & ad Dei exempla viuere debe[illegible, ~4 letters], Dan. 5. Attamen lufus iocosque hæc omnia dixeris, si eos spestes, quibus ebrietas incestuum, cædium & proprię etiam necis causa fuit. Quo nomine veteres olim illam voluntariam infaniam dixerēre: nec temerè Christus Luc. 21. de nouissimorum temporum periculis differens monet ne corda nostra ebrietate & crapula aggrauari patiamur. Nū ergo vinum corda auferre negabimus? Certè nostro seculo, proh dolor, ebrietatis vitio omnis loci & ordinis homines ita dementatos esse videmus, vt nec quotidiana damna agnoscant, nec de illis vitandis & declinandis serió cogitent. Cùm tamen non impossibile sit ab istis vitijs abstinere. Si enim Rechabitæ, si Saraceni possunt abstinere pro-fusà vino, cur Christianus non posset ab ebrietate? Beatus qui pœnitentiam egerit, & in Christi Iesu nomine peccatorum remissio nem petierit, & ab his peccatis destiterit.

page.notes: Page is clean apart from a small reference-type mark in the left margin beside the line "Rechabitæ" and a faint mark at the right margin beside "sit"; neither is printed text, so they are omitted. The word after "debe" on the line beginning "Jbat, Dan. 5." appears to be a Hebrew or decorated form and could not be read with confidence; it is marked illegible. "hará" may be "harâ" with a macron; the mark over the a is uncertain. "dixerēre" carries a macron over the e as printed. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. A small stain near the bottom left is not printed text and is omitted.
